text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian stockbrokers are set to punish petroleum products marketing firms for failing to announce their half year results by dropping their share prices, market sources say.
- The federal military government has no intention of promulgating a law to ban anyone from contesting elections, says special duties minister Wada Nas in the capital Abuja.
- Foreign shareholder of British American Insurance Nigeria Ltd, British American Holdings of London, may divest its 60 percent equity from the Nigerian firm, industry sources say.

- Central bank says budget deficit of 6.58 billion naira for first half of 1996 it reported on Wednesday was "provisional data" and that there was surplus of eight billion naira for the period as stated by finance minister Anthony Ani last month.
- Nigeria is saving $900 million annually by banning import of gypsum and exploiting local deposits of the mineral, says an official of the solid minerals ministry.
- Demand at weekly foreign exchange auction falls to $38.107 million from $42.8 million last week, says central bank.
- Oil minister Dan Etete enjoins multinational oil companies operating in Nigeria to patronise local contractors.
- Pinnacle Commercial Bank, in a press statement, debunks local newspaper reports that it is going into liquidation.
- Shell boss in Nigeria, Brian Anderson, urges massive investment in oil sector to realise goals of "Vision 2010" economic and social plan launched last month.

- Visiting president of Texaco Inc for Latin America and Africa, Eugene Celentano, pledges he will pay special attention to Nigeria because of the potential in the country's upstream sector of the oil industry.
